column2: What is the bass clef also called, and which note do its two dots surround?
column3: The F clef. The two dots surround line 4, which is F3.

column2: Name the lines of the bass staff from the bottom to the top.
Name the spaces of the bass staff from the bottom to the top.
What is the grand staff?
column3: The treble staff above the bass staff, joined by a brace and a bar line.

column2: Where is middle C (C4) written on the grand staff?
column3: On a ledger line below the treble staff, or on a ledger line above the bass staff. It is the same key.

column2: In left-hand C position, which finger is on C3 and which is on G3?
column3: Finger 5 (little finger) is on C3 and finger 1 (thumb) is on G3.

column2: Which fingers does the left hand use going up from C3 to G3?
Which left-hand finger plays E3?
column3: Finger 3 (middle finger).

column2: Do the left and right hand use the same finger numbers?
column3: Yes. Thumb = 1 and little finger = 5 in both hands.

column2: In what order do you learn a two-hand piece?
column3: Right hand alone, left hand alone, both hands at half speed, then faster in steps of 5 bpm.

column2: In a grand staff, which notes are played at the same time?
column3: Notes that line up vertically in the two staves.

column2: What is a held note?
column3: A note whose key stays down for its full length while the other hand plays.

column2: What should you do if the left hand copies the right hand's rhythm?
column3: Stop and clap the two rhythms with one hand on each knee, then go back to the keys.

column2: Which fingers and strings make the E chord?
column3: Finger 2 on string 5 fret 2, finger 3 on string 4 fret 2, finger 1 on string 3 fret 1. Play all six strings.

column2: What is the difference between the Em and E shapes?
column3: E adds finger 1 on string 3 at fret 1. Fingers 2 and 3 stay in the same place.

column2: Which fingers and strings make the A chord?
column3: Fingers 1, 2 and 3 on fret 2 of strings 4, 3 and 2. Play strings 5 to 1; do not play string 6.

column2: Spell the E major and A major chords.
column3: E major: E, G#, B. A major: A, C#, E.

column2: What is an anchor finger?
column3: A finger that stays on its string through a chord change.

column2: What does a tie do?
column3: It joins two notes of the same pitch into one long note. You play the first and hold it through the second.

column2: How many beats is a dotted half note, and why?
column3: 3 beats: a half note (2) plus half of its value (1).

column2: How many beats is a dotted quarter note?
column3: 1.5 beats: a quarter note (1) plus half of its value (0.5).

column2: How do you count eighth notes in 4/4?
column3: 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &. The numbers are the beats and the & is halfway between.

column2: How long is an eighth note, and what joins eighth notes together?
column3: Half a beat. A beam joins the stems.

column2: Which fingers and strings make the Am chord?
column3: Finger 2 on string 4 fret 2, finger 3 on string 3 fret 2, finger 1 on string 2 fret 1. Play strings 5 to 1.

column2: Which fingers and strings make the D chord, and which strings are played?
column3: Finger 1 on string 3 fret 2, finger 3 on string 2 fret 3, finger 2 on string 1 fret 2. Play strings 4 to 1 only (x x 0 2 3 2).

column2: Spell the Am and D chords.
column3: Am: A, C, E. D major: D, F#, A.

column2: What is muting by not striking?
column3: Leaving a string silent by starting the stroke on a different string, so the pick never touches it.

column2: How is the Am shape related to the E shape?
column3: Am is the E shape moved one string toward the thin strings.

column2: What does legato mean and how is it written?
column3: Smooth and connected, with no gap between notes. It is written as a slur.

column2: What does staccato mean and how is it written?
column3: Short and detached, written as a dot above or below the note head.

column2: Order p, mf and f and say what each means.
column3: p (piano) is soft, mf (mezzo forte) is medium loud, f (forte) is loud.

column2: What do an opening and a closing hairpin mean?
column3: Opening: crescendo, getting gradually louder. Closing: diminuendo, getting gradually softer.

column2: What is the difference between a tie and a slur?
column3: A tie joins two notes of the same pitch into one. A slur covers different pitches and means play legato.

column2: What does one rhythm slash in a chord chart mean?
column3: One beat. Four slashes in a 4/4 bar means a down stroke on every beat.

column2: What should you do if a chord change is too slow?
column3: Leave out the strum on beat 4 and keep the arm swinging, so the beat never stops.

column2: Where does a good down stroke start?
column3: In the forearm and wrist, with the pick sweeping across the strings in one motion.

column2: What is a chord chart?
column3: Music written as chord names above bars, usually with rhythm slashes instead of notes.

column2: What do you check when you scan a piece before sight reading?
column3: Clef, time signature, highest and lowest notes, and the rhythm. Then choose a slow tempo.

column2: What is the first rule of sight reading?
column3: Keep the beat going. Do not stop for mistakes.

column2: What do you do if you get lost while sight reading?
column3: Rejoin at the next bar line on beat 1, even if you leave out some notes.

column2: Where should your eyes be while sight reading?
column3: On the page, one beat or one bar ahead of the hands, and not on the keys.

column2: Which notes does the right hand play in G position?
column3: G4, A4, B4, C5 and D5 with fingers 1 to 5.

column2: Which notes does the left hand play in G position?
column3: G2, A2, B2, C3 and D3, with finger 5 on G2 and finger 1 on D3.

column2: Which notes does the right hand play in F position?
column3: F4, G4, A4, B4 and C5 with fingers 1 to 5.

column2: Which notes does the left hand play in F position?
column3: F2, G2, A2, B2 and C3, with finger 5 on F2 and finger 1 on C3.

column2: How can you tell which position a line is in?
column3: Find its lowest and highest notes. If they are five white keys apart, put the thumb (right hand) or little finger (left hand) on the lowest note.

column2: How does the one-minute changes exercise work?
column3: Change between two chords for 60 seconds, strumming once per chord, and count the changes where every string rang cleanly.

column2: Why only count clean changes?
column3: A sloppy change teaches a sloppy habit. The count should measure clean playing, not speed alone.

column2: Which two chords share two anchor fingers?
column3: Em and E. Fingers 2 and 3 stay on strings 5 and 4.

column2: How many changes per minute is one change every two seconds?
What does a chord symbol above a bar mean?
column3: Play that chord from where the symbol is written until the next symbol.

column2: What do A and Am mean as chord symbols?
column3: A is A major. Am is A minor.

column2: On which string does the stroke start for A, Am and D?
column3: A and Am start on string 5. D starts on string 4.

column2: How many down strokes per bar in 4/4 and in 3/4?
column3: Four in 4/4 and three in 3/4, one per beat.
